title: Independent Brownian continuum trees almost surely admit no Holder homeomorphism with exponent sufficiently close to one
source_title: Maximum agreement subtrees and Hölder homeomorphisms between Brownian trees
author: Thomas Budzinski; Delphin Sénizergues
difficulty_reason: A homeomorphism can align branch points adaptively, so mismatch at one random branch or a fixed map does not give a simultaneous obstruction for all homeomorphisms. The authors control exponentially many admissible branch-point chains and use a corrected positive-martingale mismatch argument to force uniform loss of region mass across recursive scales. Only after that new probabilistic core do Brownian excursion regularity and region-diameter bounds convert the mass loss into the strict Holder obstruction.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem2 for two independent Brownian continuum random trees with their standard excursion metrics: an existential positive exponent gap, not the displayed optional numerical10^-338 constant. Read Brownian-tree/Dirichlet definitions7–9, all recursive-decomposition and size-biased independence11–15, complete multiscale mismatch/martingale core15–25 and consecutive diameter/Holder proof25–27. Aldous three-point decomposition and Brownian-excursion small-ball/Hölder estimates are explicitly cited prior foundations. Lemma14 candidate-chain count20–21 interchanges k and ell in intermediate exponents, while ell=floor(beta*k/2) and the explicit telescoping enumeration supply an existential exponential constant; no exact K or numerical gap is selected. Proposition3 completion25 reverses the good-index complement notation in one bullet; Lemma11 explicitly defines its exponentially small bad complement. Integer floors and strict weak-mismatch threshold are bounded discretization slack in the authored Chernoff argument, no quantitative optimal constant claimed. No discrete MAST theorem or appendix homeomorphism-existence variant counted. PDF authors Thomas Budzinski and Delphin Senizergues,11/2024/256/license verified.
